title: Qualitative Codebook – Innovation Adoption in Nigerian SMEs

codes.definition: Unreliable or expensive electricity limiting operations or technology reliability.
inclusion: Generator, outages, rationing, battery replacement cost
exclusion: Energy efficiency efforts where power is adequate
codes.example: Power was killing us—diesel cost and outages.

codes.definition: Limited, unreliable, or costly internet affecting adoption or usage of digital tools.
inclusion: Dead zones, data cost, upload windows
exclusion: General IT issues not related to connectivity
codes.example: We switched to night uploads and compressed images.

codes.definition: Difficulty accessing credit or capital for adoption.
inclusion: Collateral, interest rate, cash flow timing
exclusion: Operating cost issues without financing element
codes.example: Bank wanted collateral we didn’t have.

codes.definition: Shortage of technical or managerial skills to implement and use innovation.
codes.example: Operators were scared of the dashboard.

codes.definition: Regulatory or tariff uncertainty affecting investment decisions.
codes.example: Policy risk on import duties; we diversified suppliers.

codes.definition: Customer or partner distrust hindering adoption or transactions.
codes.example: Some customers fear scams; we offer pay-on-delivery.

codes.definition: Inability to access or share data required for analytics due to privacy or business concerns.
codes.example: Merchants reluctant to share granular data.

codes.definition: Dependence on proprietary vendor ecosystems that restrict switching or data portability.
codes.example: Proprietary gateway; negotiated data export.

codes.definition: Financing structures provided by vendors enabling adoption.
codes.example: Vendor lease with maintenance.

codes.definition: Learning via peers, demos, or communities of practice.
codes.example: We did demos at market days.

codes.definition: Adapting tools and training to local language and context.
codes.example: We made Hausa guides and peer mentoring.

codes.definition: Aligning incentives to encourage adoption and compliance.
codes.example: Bonus eligibility based on safe driving and OTP deliveries.

codes.definition: Use of techniques to analyze data while maintaining privacy.
codes.example: Opt-in cohorts with clean-room style aggregates.

codes.definition: Lower operating costs attributable to the innovation.
inclusion: Fuel spend, energy per unit, logistics
codes.example: Fuel spend dropped 40%.

codes.definition: Decrease in unplanned downtime.
codes.example: Downtime fell by half.

codes.definition: Improved process control and quality metrics.
codes.example: Rejection fell from 8% to 2%.

codes.definition: Shorter lead times from order to delivery.
codes.example: Lead time down 20%.

codes.definition: Increase in sales attributable to innovation.
codes.example: Revenue grew ~18%.

codes.definition: Lower stockout frequency or depth.
codes.example: Stock-outs reduced after forecasting module.

codes.definition: Reduced spoilage or waste.
codes.example: Spoilage down 60%.

coding_rules.double_coding: Allowed when excerpt clearly spans constraint and strategy or outcome.
coding_rules.handling_quantities: Capture before/after metrics when mentioned; store as evidence objects.
coding_rules.disagreements: Resolve via coder meeting; document rationale in memo field.
